title: SSH fails instantly with "no matching cipher found" -- before any login prompt
description_md:
Connecting to this box as `deploy` fails immediately with `Unable to negotiate with ... no matching cipher found` -- there's no login prompt, no key rejection, nothing user- or key-related at all. A hardening change restricted which ciphers sshd will use, and it went further than it should have. SSH in as `trainee` (passwordless `sudo`), find the mismatch, and fix it so a normal client can actually negotiate a session -- without turning off encryption restrictions altogether.

A test key is at `~/deploy_key`. You're done when `ssh -i ~/deploy_key deploy@localhost 'echo SSH_OK'` prints `SSH_OK`.
